claims.summary: A fresh deployed v0.15.132 UX Studio ZIP/log audit regraded 99/100 with the only scored loss in assessment identity while source proof, export verification, and texture were otherwise clean enough.
The remaining P2 was a compiler mismatch where the Course Map and manifest carried 36 assessment rows but the blueprint compiler authored 12 assignment briefs from the native graph registry.
proofCommands: rg -n "36 assessment rows|12 assignment briefs|23 course-map assessments" docs/V0.15.133_ASSESSMENT_REGISTRY_BRIDGE_ROADMAP.md

claims.summary: Generation bridges the richer visible Course Map assessment registry into the blueprint compiler when it has more rows than the native graph so promised graded checkpoints produce downstream artifacts.
The semantic compiler contract accepts registry-mode multi-anchor lessons while still blocking gradeable registry rows whose lessons have no compiled assessment anchor.

Focused registry regressions prove a native one-assessment graph plus a visible three-assessment Course Map compiles three assignment briefs and clears assessment reconciliation without weakening standards.

knownRemainingTargets: Fresh deployed v0.15.133 ZIP/log audit must prove the Course Map assessment registry bridge works in real provider output.
The next package must show that all gradeable Course Map assessment rows have matching dedicated assignment or exam artifacts.

Fresh provider evidence must still prove overall 100/100, Texture 100/100 or no scored texture loss, no hidden source/review/export caveats, and agreement across UI, ZIP, manifest, reports, digest logs, and local regrade.
Source rows must remain real, trusted, on-topic, license-safe, and concept-linked across UX and Project Management domains.
